meaning: A way to train a policy from its own scored attempts at a task, so that it can become better than the demonstrations it started from.
A number that scores an attempt or one step of an attempt. For example, the reward can be 1 when the block ends in the cup and 0 otherwise.
One try at the task by the current policy. It is an episode in which the policy drives the arm instead of a person.
One decision by the policy and the motion that follows it. In the SO-101 vision task, one control step covers 20 physics steps.
In the VLA recipes, one round of collecting attempts and updating the model. It is a much larger unit than a control step.
An RL algorithm that alternates between collecting a batch of fresh attempts and making a limited update of the policy from that batch.
PPO's limit on how far the probability of an action may move away from the policy that collected the batch. Past that limit, the change earns nothing more in the objective.
An RL algorithm that scores each attempt against the other attempts collected with it.
A program that computes how the arm and the objects around it move, so that an attempt needs no hardware.
One simulated copy of the scene, such as an arm, a table and a cube. A GPU advances thousands of environments in one batch.
Computing the image that a camera in the simulated scene would see.
Running a policy trained in simulation on the real arm with no further training.
Inputs given to the policy as numbers, such as joint angles and object positions, with no image.
A plain stack of fully connected layers.
A large pretrained model that reads camera images and a text instruction and outputs a chunk of future actions.
The image-and-text network that a VLA is built on.
A second model that looks at the current moment of an attempt and predicts how well the attempt will end.
The outcome that followed an action minus the outcome that the value function predicted. It measures how much better or worse than expected the attempt went.

A training method that labels each recorded action as better or worse than expected and trains the policy on all of them with the label as an extra input. At run time, the policy is asked for the better label.

expansion: RL with Experience and Corrections via Advantage-conditioned Policies
meaning: Physical Intelligence's method for improving a VLA from its own attempts and from human corrections.
A suite of simulated manipulation tasks used as a benchmark.
RL run directly on a real arm. It starts from a few demonstrations, and a person takes over to correct attempts that are going wrong.
The program that runs the current policy on the arm and sends what happened to the learner.
The program that stores transitions, does the gradient updates on a GPU and sends new weights to the actor.
The record of one step: the observation, the action, the reward and the next observation.
A store of past transitions that training samples from again and again.
An RL method that trains from a replay buffer, so that each real step is reused in many updates.
Putting the scene back to its starting state between attempts.
A person taking over the arm for a moment during an autonomous attempt. The person's action replaces the policy's action and is stored with the rest of the data.
The average of a judge's detection rate on successes and its detection rate on failures. A score of 0.5 means chance.
Changing the simulated arm and scene at the start of every episode, so that the real arm falls inside the range of conditions the policy trained on.
A GPU's ordinary arithmetic units, as opposed to its tensor cores or its ray-tracing cores.
